research_question: Is sustained-attention task score associated with a triadic connectivity index across a fixture cohort of forty participants?
falsifiability_criteria: If the association is not significant after false-discovery-rate correction at alpha 0.05, the hypothesis is falsified.
primary_endpoint: Pearson correlation between the triadic connectivity index and the sustained-attention score
secondary_endpoints: pairwise connectivity as a comparison baseline
alternative_explanations: head motion could inflate connectivity estimates

condition_label_definitions.task: sustained attention task with visual targets

null_model.description: Fourier phase randomization preserving the power spectrum, 1000 surrogates

leakage_controls: subject-level split enforced before any preprocessing
known_leakage_risks: repeated sessions from one subject could leak identity across folds

split_strategy.method: five-fold grouped cross-validation by subject identifier

measurement_limitations: temporal resolution limits detection of fast dynamics
claim_language: We hypothesize an association between the connectivity index and sustained attention; this is a correlational, exploratory analysis.
replication_plan: Replicate on an independent held-out cohort before any confirmatory claim.

privacy_measures: access restricted to the study team
